### R Workflow and Examples

Run the examples in order because later blocks may reuse objects created earlier. Each block includes a short purpose statement and guidance for reading its output.


<!-- generated-learning-note -->
**Purpose.** This source block depends on optional software, external data, or a machine-specific path. It is retained as a reference and is not executed during the website build.

```{r leaflet, warning=FALSE}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
# Get data:
library(gapminder)

# load libraries:
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)

# create text label 
gapminder$countrylabel <- ifelse(gapminder$country=="United States", 'US',
                    ifelse(gapminder$country=="China", "CN", ""))

# Make a ggplot, but add frame=year: one image per year
# add text at top of specific points
ggplot(gapminder, aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, size = pop, color = continent)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_bw() +
  # gganimate specific bits:
  labs(title = 'Year: {frame_time}', x = 'GDP per capita', y = 'life expectancy') +
  transition_time(year) +
  ease_aes('linear')+
  geom_text(data=gapminder, aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, label=gapminder$countrylabel, fill=1, vjust = -0.5 ))

# Save at gif:
# anim_save("C:\\Users\\hed2\\gganimate1.gif")

```

#### Wordcloud

<!-- generated-learning-note -->
This subsection explains **Wordcloud** and shows how it contributes to the overall How to create advanced plots workflow.


<!-- generated-learning-note -->
**Purpose.** This source block depends on optional software, external data, or a machine-specific path. It is retained as a reference and is not executed during the website build.

```{r , warning=FALSE}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
# load Packages
require(RColorBrewer)
require(tidyverse)
require(magrittr)
require(ggwordcloud)

library(SnowballC)
library(tm)

# load text data using a filter() function from dplyr package
# devtools::install_github("JohnCoene/sacred")
scripture = sacred::king_james_version

john = scripture %>% 
  filter(book == "joh")%>% 
  select(text)

# transforming the text document into corpus
john.corpus = john %>% 
  tm::VectorSource() %>% 
  tm::VCorpus()

# replacing special characters to space
toSpace = content_transformer(function (x , pattern ) 
  gsub(pattern, " ", x))

john.corpus = john.corpus %>% 
  tm_map(toSpace, "/") %>%
  tm_map(toSpace, " ") %>%
  tm_map(toSpace, "\\|")

# removing stopwords and change all words to small letters
john.corpus =  john.corpus %>% 
  tm_map(FUN = content_transformer(tolower)) %>% # Convert the text to lower case
  tm_map(FUN = removeNumbers) %>% # Remove numbers
  tm_map(removeWords, stopwords("english")) %>% # Remove english common stopwords
  tm_map(removeWords, c("ye", "O", "unto", "yet", "thee", "wherein", "neither", "shall", 
                        "saith", "host", "will", "offer", "say")) %>%   # Remove words
  tm_map(removePunctuation) %>%   # Remove punctuations
  tm_map(stripWhitespace)   #

 

# compute the frequency of each word
# changed from corpus format to matrix and to data.frame
john.corpus.tb=  john.corpus %>% 
  tm::TermDocumentMatrix(control = list(removeNumbers = TRUE,
                                        stopwords = TRUE,
                                        stemming = TRUE)) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
  dplyr::rename(word = 1, freq = 2) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(freq))


# make the word cloud 
john.corpus.tb[1,1]="Yeshua"

set.seed(42)
ggplot(
  john.corpus.tb,
  aes(
    label = word, size = freq,
    color =  (freq)
  )
) +
  geom_text_wordcloud_area(aes(angle = 45 * sample(-2:2, nrow(john.corpus.tb),
                                                   replace = TRUE,
                                                   prob = c(1, 1, 4, 1, 1)
  )),
  mask = png::readPNG("C:\\Users\\hed2\\Downloads\\mask.png"
  ),
  rm_outside = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 20) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # scale_color_brewer(palette = "Paired", direction = -1)
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "darkred")
 
```

```{r,eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
# customize the map levels 
df <- data.frame(
  location_name = c("点击放大+",
                    "He",
                    "使用我",
                    "用这种方式",
                    "跟你说话",
                    "这也是我刚学会的",
                    "（M 7:7）",
                    "“Ask",
                    "and it will be given to you;",
                    "seek",
                    "and you will find;",
                    "knock",
                    "and the door will be opened to you.",
                    "He",
                    "Still",
                    "Love You",
                    "因为他从来没有忘记，每天早上要叫醒你。",
                    "Remember: ",
                    "When He is going to do something amazing, He always starts with an impossibility."),
  lng = c(-77.13120125000563),
  lat = c(39.05904434957069), 
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
  
ui <- shinyUI(
  fluidPage(
    leafletOutput(outputId = 'map')
  )
)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>%
      addTiles()
  })
  
  observeEvent(
    eventExpr = input$map_zoom, {
      print(input$map_zoom)           # Display zoom level in the console
      leafletProxy(
        mapId = "map", 
        session = session
      ) %>% 
        clearMarkers() %>%
        addMarkers(
          data = df, 
          lng = ~lng,
          lat = ~lat,
          labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = T,
                                      textOnly = T,
                                      style = list(
                                        "color" = "blue",
                                        "font-size" = "18px")   ),
                                     
          label = if(input$map_zoom == 0){
            ~location_name[1]
            }else if(input$map_zoom == 1){
            ~location_name[2]
            } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 2){
      ~location_name[3]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 3){
      ~location_name[4]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 4){
      ~location_name[5]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 5){
      ~location_name[6]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 6){
      ~location_name[7]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 7){
      ~location_name[8]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 8){
      ~location_name[9]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 9){
      ~location_name[10]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 10){
      ~location_name[11]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 11){
      ~location_name[12]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 12){
      ~location_name[13]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 13){
      ~location_name[14]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 14){
      ~location_name[15]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 15){
      ~location_name[16]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 16){
      ~location_name[17]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 17){
      ~location_name[18]
    } 
    else if(input$map_zoom == 18){
      ~location_name[19]
    } 
 
        )
    }
  )
  
})

shinyApp(
  ui = ui, 
  server = server
)
```

## Interpreting the Results

Use summaries and visual checks to confirm ranges, distributions, duplicates, and missing-data patterns. Treat the output as evidence generated under the stated data, coding choices, and assumptions. Before using the workflow in practice, replace example inputs with validated data and confirm that the method targets the intended scientific question.

## Key Takeaways

- **Connect method to purpose.** Identify the question and target quantity before choosing code or a model.
- **Read code and output together.** Confirm what each object, estimate, interval, table, or plot represents.
- **Check assumptions and diagnostics.** A successful computation is not by itself evidence that the result is reliable.
- **Adapt deliberately.** When applying the example elsewhere, document changes to data definitions, parameters, and analytical choices.
